extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, patent prosecutors, and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner practice for claiming and proving foreign priority in U.S. patent applications (timing, required content, certified copies, petitions for delayed or restored priority, and electronic retrieval). Applies to original 35 U.S.C. 111(a) applications, national stage (35 U.S.C. 371) filings, and design applications where noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim for priority presentation and required identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim for priority must be presented in an application data sheet (§ 1.76(b)(6)) (for applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a)), and must identify the foreign application to which priority is claimed by specifying the application number, country (or intellectual property authority), day, month, and year of its filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after September 16, 2012 the claim must be in an application data sheet. For applications filed prior to that date, unless provided in an ADS, the oath or declaration under 37 CFR 1.63 must identify the foreign application. Proper and complete identification is essential for electronic retrieval under PDX; use WIPO-recommended presentation (see MPEP § 214.04 and WIPO Handbook Part 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for claiming priority (37 CFR 1.55(d)(1) and (d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: For original applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) (other than design applications), the claim for priority and required identification must be filed during the pendency of the application and within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application. For national stage applications under 35 U.S.C. 371, the claim must be made within the time limit set forth in the PCT and PCT Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time period in 37 CFR 1.55(d) for non-design applications is not extendable. If the claim is not timely, it is considered waived unless accepted under the unintentionally delayed claim procedures (37 CFR 1.55(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Design application exception (37 CFR 1.55(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods in 37 CFR 1.55(d) do not apply to design applications; in a design application, a claim for priority may be made at any time during the pendency of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective May 13, 2015 37 CFR 1.55(e) allows petitions to accept unintentionally delayed priority claims in design applications where the foreign priority claim was not submitted during pendency. Such petitions may be filed with a request for certificate of correction after grant. See MPEP § 216.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unintentionally delayed priority claim — petition content (37 CFR 1.55(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition to accept a delayed claim for priority must be accompanied by: (1) the priority claim in an application data sheet identifying the foreign application unless previously submitted; (2) a certified copy of the foreign application, unless previously submitted or an exception applies; (3) the petition fee as set forth in § 1.17(m); and (4) a statement that the entire delay between the date the priority claim was due and the date it was filed was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question whether the delay was unintentional. If the petition is filed more than two years after the foreign priority claim was due, additional explanation of the surrounding circumstances establishing that the entire delay was unintentional is required (85 FR 12222-24). Separate procedures apply for design applications and for claims filed after issue (certificate of correction plus petition).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy requirement and meaning (35 U.S.C.119(b)(3); 37 CFR 1.55)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office requires a certified copy of the foreign priority application pursuant to 37 CFR 1.55; the certified copy is a copy of the original foreign application with a certification by the foreign patent office (ordinarily the specification and drawings as filed plus certificate information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy of the printed foreign patent does not comply unless the certification indicates it corresponds to the application as filed. An applicant's copy filed via USPTO e-filing does not satisfy the 37 CFR 1.55(g) certified-copy requirement. Examiners should review certified copies for obvious formal defects and correspondence to the identified foreign application (number, date, country).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copy filed in parent or related U.S. patent/application satisfies requirement (37 CFR 1.55(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for a certified copy will be considered satisfied if a certified copy of the foreign application has already been filed in a parent U.S. patent or prior nonprovisional application for which benefit is claimed and that application is identified as containing the certified copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may simply identify the parent application containing the certified copy. Examiner should acknowledge the claim (form PTOL-326) and may notify applicant using form paragraph 2.20 if necessary. If the applicant fails to identify that the certified copy is in the parent but the examiner is aware, the examiner should call attention to that fact in an Office action so priority data will appear in the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper identification format of foreign application numbers (MPEP § 214.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should present foreign application numbers using the recommended presentations in the WIPO Handbook (Part 7) and use the 'Minimum Significant Part of the Number' identified in the WIPO tables to ensure accurate citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the WIPO tables for each intellectual property office to extract the minimum required data to form a proper citation. Improper, incomplete, or inconsistent citations will delay or prevent electronic retrieval under the Priority Document Exchange program. Applicants are strongly encouraged to use an acceptable format and be consistent throughout the U.S. application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Priority Document Exchange (PDX) retrieval practice and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A proper priority claim to an application filed in a participating foreign intellectual property office is treated as a request for the USPTO to obtain a copy from that office via PDX; the Office will attempt retrieval when the application is docketed to an examiner and after the Office of Patent Application Processing completes review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retrieval typically takes about one week. If an eligible foreign application is filed in a participating office, the USPTO will attempt retrieval; for certain receiving offices and if the WIPO DAS access code is provided, retrieval of international/PCT applications is automatic. If retrieval fails or the foreign application was not originally in a participating office, applicant may file Form PTO/SB/38 to request retrieval. Successful retrieval is not guaranteed; check Patent Center to confirm. Retrieval requires accurate citation format; incomplete claims prevent electronic retrieval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office acknowledgement and examiner communication (form paragraphs and when to use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should use specific form paragraphs to notify applicants of priority claim status: e.g., ¶2.21.01 for untimely foreign priority claims, ¶2.26 (PTOL-326) to acknowledge timely certified copies, ¶2.27 to acknowledge a certified copy filed in a parent, ¶2.23 where foreign filing was more than 12 months earlier with no restoration, ¶2.22 where certified copy does not correspond to the identified priority claim or proper claim not made, and ¶2.25 when certified copy not filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes in the MPEP specify usage limitations (e.g., do not use certain paragraphs for design applications). Bracketed fields in the form paragraphs indicate insertion of dates, application numbers, or country names as appropriate. Examiners should follow the MPEP guidance for which paragraph to use in each situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filing more than 12 months earlier; restoration petition (37 CFR 1.55(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the earlier foreign application was filed more than 12 months prior to the U.S. application and priority has not been restored under PCT Rule 26bis.3 or a petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c) granted, priority cannot be based on that earlier filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c) to restore the right of priority if the subsequent application was filed within two months from the expiration of the twelve-month period and the delay was unintentional. A petition to restore must include: (1) the priority claim in an ADS identifying the foreign application; (2) the petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(m); and (3) a statement that the delay in filing the subsequent application within the twelve-month period was unintentional. The Director may require additional information where there is a question about unintentionality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of filing priority papers after payment of issue fee or after issue (certificate of correction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority claims and certified copies filed after payment of the issue fee but before grant will be placed in the application file but may not be reviewed, and the issued patent may not include the priority claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To have the foreign priority claim considered after publication/grant, a certificate of correction under 35 U.S.C. 255 and 37 CFR 1.323 can be filed; for original 35 U.S.C. 111(a) and national stage (371) applications, a grantable petition to accept an unintentionally delayed claim under 37 CFR 1.55(e) and the petition fee must be filed with the certificate of correction. Certified copies entered into the file will not be returned to applicant.
